channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Range trade persists, downside risk intact against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Senior Technical Strategist Quek Ser Leang expects USD/CNH to remain confined in a tight near-term range, with the Dollar likely to trade between 6.7950 and 6.8100. Despite easing upward momentum, UOB still sees scope for a move toward 6.8300 while 6.7900 holds as strong support.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar eases ahead of US jobs data, ECB Forum and China PMIs
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) lost some momentum on Monday, trading near 101.10 but remaining close to recent highs, as investors took profits ahead of key US labor market data later in the week.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG stays below $60 as death cross threat looms
item.description: Silver price treads water, losing over 1.50% as the white metal is poised to end June down over 22.50% after tumbling below $60.00 per troy ounce. The rise in US Treasury yields, the strength of the US Dollar, and the lack of a geopolitical risk premium keep the non-yielding metal pressured.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Dollar strength threatens APAC FX – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights renewed US Dollar (USD) strength as a growing headwind for APAC (Asia-Pacific) currencies, with USD/JPY identified as the pivotal pair.

item.title: Euro: Political and growth risks point lower against US Dollar – HSBC
item.description: HSBC notes that dovish comments from European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde and lower Oil prices now lead its economists to expect the ECB to hold rates in 2026.

item.title: ECB’s Lagarde: ECB can raise rates to address inflation without fear
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde delivered an introductory speech at the ECB Forum on Central Banking 2026 on Monday, warning that the Eurozone is likely to face more frequent shocks in the coming years that could move inflation away from the ECB’s target.

item.title: US Treasury yields steady as Fed hike bets offset Oil calm
item.description: US Treasury yields steadied on Monday during the North American session as tensions in the Middle East halted the decline in crude Oil prices, while money markets are still pricing in at least 34 basis points of Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening in 2026.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Corrective pressure points lower – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the US Dollar (USD) is easing for a third straight session as Fed hike expectations fade, with swaps now pricing less than 20bps of tightening by September.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Consolidates near recent lows against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes USD/SGD slipped to 1.2929 before recovering, with intraday price action still seen as range trading. For the day, the pair is expected to stay between 1.2930 and 1.2960.

item.title: Gold price slides as easing US-Iran tensionsdent haven demand
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price retreats by some 1.50% on Monday as risk appetite improves following the halt of hostilities over the weekend between the US and Iran, which threatened to derail negotiations and Oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Euro strengthens as Eurozone sentiment improves ahead of German HICP
item.description: EUR/USD rose above 1.1420 in the American session on Monday as investors digested mixed Eurozone sentiment figures and looked ahead to key German data. The latest Eurozone releases showed Business Climate in June at -0.38, weaker than the previous revised -0.27 reading.

item.title: Canadian Dollar consolidates amid Oil price rebound, US labor data in focus
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.4210 on Monday at the time of writing, as investors remain on the sidelines ahead of a series of key US labor market releases, culminating with Thursday's June Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report.

item.title: British Pound rises as Burnham fiscal pledge calms markets
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) advances 0.40% on Monday after Andy Burnham, who is expected to become the new UK Prime Minister, commented that he will adhere to fiscal rules set by Chancellor Rachel Reeves at a speech in which he laid the path for the economy.

item.title: British Pound: Leadership turmoil and weaker carry weigh on Sterling – HSBC
item.description: HSBC argues that the Pound is more exposed to downside risks following Prime Minister Starmer’s resignation and the ensuing UK leadership contest.

item.title: Asian FX: Vulnerable under risk-off and stronger Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong expect Asian FX to start the week on a softer footing as AI-led equity losses and renewed US–Iran tensions keep the Dollar bid.

item.title: Australian Dollar slips near three-month low as traders await RBA Minutes
item.description: AUD/USD trades near the 0.6880 level on Monday, down from Friday's close as traders await fresh catalysts from Australia and China.

item.title: Euro: Range trading likely to persist against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note EUR/USD is holding within a short-term channel as markets await comments from ECB President Lagarde at the Sintra symposium, which historically has had limited impact on near-term price action.

item.title: Silver declines as Middle East energy tensions, Fed policy uncertainty pressure prices
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) is down 2.37% on Monday, trading around $57.75 at the time of writing, as investors reassess the impact of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East on energy markets and the inflation outlook.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: China slowdown weighs on CNY against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao highlight that China’s industrial profit growth slowed to 21.1% year-on-year in May, with weaker consumption and investment pointing to easing momentum.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Japan export controls and strong sales support JPY risk premium – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that China has expanded its export control list to include more Japanese entities, raising supply chain risks for defense and rare earths, while Japanese commercial sales grew strongly in May.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Stabilizes against US Dollar as spreads narrow – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Canadian Dollar (CAD) has gained modest relief as front-end US/Canada spreads retreat about 10bps from last week’s peak, though rate differentials remain punitive.

item.title: Kevin Warsh isn't expected to say much in Sintra: That's exactly why markets will listen
item.description: Financial markets could find an important catalyst in the enchanting, fairytale-like landscape of Sintra this week. The European Central Bank (ECB) Forum will, as it does every year, gather the crème de la crème of central banks.

item.title: US Dollar: Cyclical drivers and de-dollarisation – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley examines structural de-dollarisation themes alongside near-term Dollar dynamics. The de-dollarisation debate intensified after tariffs failed to trigger a traditional safe-haven bid for the Dollar and Treasuries in April 2025.

item.title: Euro: Sintra seasonality points to tactical strength against US Dollar – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights a recurring post-Sintra pattern in the Euro, with hawkish ECB communication from Christine Lagarde typically driving EUR/USD gains from late June into early July before they fade.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Downtrend tests 2024 low against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux highlights that USD/JPY has broken out of a brief consolidation and is now challenging its 2024 peak near 162.00. The bank notes strong May retail sales support expectations for further Bank of Japan tightening.

item.title: Eurozone: Heatwaves add macro risk for growth – ING
item.description: ING’s Global Head of Macro Carsten Brzeski warns that recurring European heatwaves are becoming a structural drag on Eurozone growth. He cites academic and ECB research showing measurable losses in output and higher food inflation linked to extreme temperatures.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Fed hikes repriced on softer inflation – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank Research notes that investors reduced expectations for further Fed rate hikes after softer US PCE inflation, pulling December hike pricing down and lowering 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields.

item.title: Euro: Cyclical Dollar strength versus EUR risks – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses EUR/USD within a broader reassessment of Dollar drivers. Foley notes that even if the US Dollar (USD) is in long-term decline, cyclical forces can still support it.

item.title: British Pound gains as UK Burnham pledges continuation of current Labour policy
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) outperforms its major currency peers, trading 0.25% higher to near 1.3230 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Monday.

item.title: Oil: Gulf de-escalation keeps crude supported – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu reports that the U.S. and Iran have agreed to halt mutual attacks and resume talks on the Strait of Hormuz, allowing shipping to move more freely. Markets reacted cautiously, with Brent, WTI and Omani crude prices higher as tensions eased.
